06. TURNING ANALYSIS INTO EFFECTIVE VISUAL COMMUNICATION_

Five important A05 findings, redesigned as clear static figures for the research paper. Every section preserves the original visualization and explains the design decisions.

[6.1] FROM EXPLORATION TO PAPER FIGURES

The A05 plots were designed to inspect data. These redesigned figures emphasize a specific finding, with titles, explicit units, meaningful scales, direct annotations, and captions that stand on their own.

Redesigned figures use the website’s dark green backgrounds, bright green accents, and monospace typography. Clear labels, honest scales, and restrained annotations keep them suitable as research figures within the same visual theme. Every figure includes a descriptive SVG title, a text alternative, an exact-data table, and a research implication.

The data and conclusions are unchanged. All figures use A05’s 285 retained records after the earlier exclusion of 103 matching rows. Without person IDs, that exclusion is an assumption. Output records Yes/No, not order frequency; income remains categorical INR brackets. No dates, hypothesis tests, or uncertainty intervals are invented.

BEFORE · ORIGINAL ASSIGNMENT 5 VISUALIZATION

↓ REDESIGNED FOR CLEARER COMMUNICATION ↓

AFTER · RESEARCH-PAPER FIGURE

Text alternative: Directly labeled dot plot of Yes rates by marital status, showing Single 84.7%, Married 60.9%, and Prefer not to say 44.4%. The latter group has only 9 records.

SQ1: marital-status comparison: The observed Single–Married gap motivates analysis that also accounts for age and occupation; the figure does not establish a marital-status effect.

[6.5] FIGURE 4 · Ordering and feedback show the strongest pairwise link

A05 V07 → A06 FIGURE 4

BEFORE · ORIGINAL ASSIGNMENT 5 VISUALIZATION

↓ REDESIGNED FOR CLEARER COMMUNICATION ↓

AFTER · RESEARCH-PAPER FIGURE

Text alternative: Coefficient plot of six signed correlations on a minus-one to plus-one axis. Ordering and positive feedback have the largest absolute correlation, about +0.55.

SQ2 / SQ3: relationships: The ordering–feedback association is descriptive. Feedback timing is unknown and should not automatically become a predictor of a prior ordering decision.

DESIGN JUSTIFICATION · CHART, TITLE, LABELS, SCALE, LEGEND, ANNOTATION, LAYOUT & ACCESSIBILITY
DESIGN ELEMENTWHAT CHANGED AND WHY
Chart typeReplace the redundant 4×4 matrix with a ranked coefficient plot of six unique variable pairs.
TitleCall out the strongest observed pair without suggesting a predictive or causal effect.
LabelsName both variables in every row and print the signed correlation next to its point.
ScaleUse the full theoretical −1 to +1 correlation range with a visible zero reference.
LegendEliminate a colorbar; left/right position, signed labels, and amber/cyan accents show direction.
AnnotationExplain that correlations are pairwise; binary variables use 0/1 coding.
Layout / hierarchyRemove duplicate cells and self-correlations; order pairs by absolute magnitude.
AccessibilitySigned text and spatial position carry meaning without color; provide the exact six-pair table.

[6.7] FIGURE SELECTION & CONSISTENT DESIGN RULES

PAPER FIGUREA05 SOURCEVISUAL COMMUNICATION GOAL
1V01Most retained records describe adults under 30
2V03Single records have a higher observed Yes rate
3V05The No Income category has the highest Yes rate
4V07Ordering and feedback show the strongest pairwise link
5V09Positive feedback is more common among Single records

Distributions keep their original binning; rates use full 0–100% scales; correlations use the full −1 to +1 range. Sample sizes and definitions accompany the figures. Direct text and position convey meaning alongside color. No chart uses 3D, decorative icons, or invented numerical income values.

The correlation redesign removes duplicate cells and self-correlations but preserves all six unique pairwise values. The feedback redesign retains a composition chart because it already suits the question; orientation, labels, title, and hierarchy are improved.

[6.8] EXPORTS & REPRODUCIBILITY

The complete package contains five original SVGs, five redesigned vector SVGs, five 300-dpi PNGs, exact-data CSVs, captions, saved A05 results, and a reproducible Python script. The page embeds all ten figures. Redesigned charts use self-contained high-resolution images so external SVG styling cannot override their green terminal palette. No chart library or JavaScript is required.
